title: Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus
summary: We discussed whether men and women are really different, and talked about stereotypes, gender roles and peer pressure. We practised agreeing and disagreeing politely, and we used tentative language (tend to, it seems that, it could be argued) to avoid over-generalisations.

vocab.def: Thinking that all people in a group are the same, often unfairly.
vocab.example: Amy thinks there is still a lot of stereotyping about what boys and girls should like.

fr.d: fille qui aime les jeux, vêtements et activités qu'on pense être pour les garçons

vocab.example: My aunt is so loquacious that nobody else can say a word at dinner.

ar.d: يتكلم كثيراً ويحب الحديث

de.d: redet viel und gern

es.d: que habla mucho y le gusta hablar

fr.d: qui parle beaucoup et aime parler

vocab.def: Angry and ready to fight or argue.

ar.d: غاضب ومستعد للشجار أو الجدال

de.d: wütend und bereit zu kämpfen oder zu streiten

es.d: enfadado y dispuesto a pelear o discutir

fr.d: en colère et prêt à se battre ou à se disputer

de.d: jemanden an seinem Gedächtnis oder Gefühl zweifeln lassen, um ihn zu kontrollieren

ar.d: التذمّر من أخطاء أو تفاصيل صغيرة جداً وغير مهمة

es.d: quejarse de errores o detalles muy pequeños y sin importancia

fr.d: se plaindre de toutes petites erreurs ou de détails sans importance

zh.d: 善于找到快速又聪明的方法解决问题

es.d: bueno para encontrar formas rápidas e inteligentes de resolver problemas

grammar.title: Tentative language (avoiding over-generalisations)
grammar.explain: When we have no strong evidence, we don't say 'All women...' or 'Men always...'. We use softer, tentative language to show that something is often true, but not always. This makes our opinion sound fair and polite.
grammar.explain_ar: عندما لا يكون لدينا دليل قوي، لا نقول «كل النساء...» أو «الرجال دائماً...». بل نستخدم لغة أكثر حذراً وليونة لنُظهر أن الأمر صحيح في كثير من الأحيان وليس دائماً، فيبدو رأينا منصفاً ومهذباً.
form: subject + tend to + base verb (Women tend to live longer.)
It seems that / It appears that + clause
It could be argued that / You could argue that + clause
subject + be + more likely to + base verb
frequency adverbs: usually, often, generally (before the main verb)

examples.en: Women tend to be better at learning languages than men.
examples.note: Softer than 'All women are better at languages'.

examples.en: Generally speaking, women are expected to spend more on beauty products than men.
examples.note: 'Generally speaking' shows this is true in general, not for everyone.

examples.en: It could be argued that it is more acceptable for women to cry in public than men.
examples.note: Passive 'could be argued': we present the idea without saying it is a fact.

examples.en: It appears that women have better memories than men.
A primary school teacher is more likely to be a woman.
examples.note: 'more likely to' talks about probability, not certainty.

mistakes.wrong: All men are bad at cooking.
mistakes.right: Men tend to cook less often than women.
mistakes.why: Avoid over-generalisations with 'all', 'always', 'never' when you have no evidence.

mistakes.wrong: Women tend being better at languages.
mistakes.right: Women tend to be better at languages.

mistakes.wrong: It could argued that boys are noisier.
mistakes.right: It could be argued that boys are noisier.
mistakes.why: It is passive: could + be + past participle.

mistakes.wrong: A nurse is more likely be a woman.
mistakes.right: A nurse is more likely to be a woman.

mistakes.wrong: It seems women that live longer.
mistakes.right: It seems that women live longer.
mistakes.why: 'That' comes straight after 'It seems', before the clause.

quiz.q: Parents ___ choose toys based on their child's gender.
quiz.why: We use 'tend to' + base verb for general habits.

options: All girls get better grades than boys.
Girls always get better grades than boys.
Girls often get better grades than boys.
quiz.why: 'Often' softens the statement; 'all' and 'always' are over-generalisations.

quiz.q: It could be ___ that men and women are equally good at multitasking.
quiz.why: Passive form: could be + past participle (argued).

quiz.q: A primary school teacher is more ___ to be a woman.
quiz.why: The phrase is 'more likely to + base verb'.

quiz.q: ___ speaking, women are expected to spend more on beauty products.
It ___ that more domestic helpers are women.

grammar.title: Giving a contrasting opinion: although, even though, on the other hand
grammar.explain: We use these words to show two ideas that are different or surprising together. 'Although' and 'even though' join two clauses in one sentence. 'On the other hand' starts a new sentence with the opposite idea.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم هذه الكلمات لربط فكرتين متعارضتين أو مفاجئتين. «although» و«even though» (مع أنّ / رغم أنّ) تربطان جملتين في جملة واحدة، أما «on the other hand» (من ناحية أخرى) فتبدأ بها جملة جديدة تحمل الفكرة المعاكسة.
form: Although / Even though + clause, + main clause
Main clause + although / even though + clause
Sentence. On the other hand, + sentence.
I see your point, but + clause / People say that, but + clause

examples.en: Although many people think boys are noisier, my daughter is much louder than my son.
examples.note: The second idea is surprising after the first.

examples.en: Even though she is a girl, she loves football and video games.
examples.note: 'Even though' is a little stronger than 'although'.

examples.en: Boys often like cars. On the other hand, many girls enjoy them too.
examples.note: 'On the other hand' starts a new sentence, followed by a comma.

examples.en: I see your point, but that's not always the case.

mistakes.wrong: Although he is a boy, but he likes dolls.
mistakes.right: Although he is a boy, he likes dolls.
mistakes.why: Don't use 'but' together with 'although' in the same sentence.

mistakes.wrong: Even though the stereotypes, girls can be engineers.
mistakes.right: Even though there are stereotypes, girls can be engineers.
mistakes.why: 'Even though' needs a full clause with a subject and a verb.

mistakes.wrong: Men are strong, on the other hand women are strong too.
mistakes.right: Men are strong. On the other hand, women are strong too.
mistakes.why: 'On the other hand' usually starts a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

mistakes.wrong: Even although she is tired, she works hard.
mistakes.right: Even though she is tired, she works hard.

quiz.q: ___ women usually live longer, men often work in more dangerous jobs.
quiz.why: 'Although' joins two clauses in one sentence.

options: Although he's shy, but he talks a lot at home.
Although he's shy, he talks a lot at home.
Although shy, but he talks a lot at home.

quiz.q: Girls often get better grades. ___, boys sometimes do better in maths tests.
quiz.why: 'On the other hand' starts a new sentence with a contrasting idea.

quiz.q: ___ she grew up with four brothers, she is a real girly girl.
I see your point, ___ that isn't always like that.
quiz.why: The fixed phrase is 'I see your point, but...'.

phrases.use: Disagreeing: bringing in a different example

phrases.en: It could also be said that ...

phrases.use: Disagreeing politely after accepting the other view

phrases.en: Well, I know what you're saying, but ...
Yes, I've noticed that as well.
Women are valued by / cherished by / treasured by us.
They hit boys to discipline them.
phrases.use: Teacher's correction: 'discipline them', not 'make them act correct'
